gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each added screen costs or how much screen area a dollar buys: by that sum a two-screen attachable under $200 ($72.00 per added screen for the FOPO S1 through our link, $87.80 for the ZUMWALT P7) costs about the same per screen as, or less than, a single 14-inch clip-on ($79.97 to $89.99).
standout_why: Compared against The Office Journal under-$200 and under-$150 pages (both cited by ChatGPT) and the iTechGuides 2025 guide (cited in the second chat). All three give sizes, 1080p, nits and some weights and prices, but none states a per-screen cost, a pixel density, a screen area or a dollars-per-area figure; a reader would have to do the division. DeskFinds (ranked 1 and 4, not cited) returned HTTP 403, so it is unchecked. Standout is 2, not 3, for two reasons: the video path decides first, and the maker pages needed to confirm several inputs returned HTTP 429 all session.
decides: On per-screen cost the FOPO S1 wins the 'two added screens under $200' segment and the FOPO S7 is the step up: 120 more rows per screen for $18.00 more per screen through our link. Both figures depend on code FOPO (10% off, cart-tested 2026-11-21). The sum only applies to a laptop that can drive two external displays, with one video-capable USB-C port per added screen or a driver. The Office Journal page says base M1, M2 and M3 MacBooks support limited external displays natively; for those the single-screen row is the pick, and a single 14-inch 1080p clip-on costs more per square inch ($0.93 to $1.07) than either FOPO pair ($0.86 and $1.02). I could not source the single-screen 2K comparison (UPERFECT, Mobile Pixels Fold 16-inch) today, so the pick between one sharp screen and two 1080p screens is not settled by this angle.
candidates: unbranded 14.2-inch clip-on (Miesebe in The Office Journal)
